title: upfly dedupe --json: the result
description: The last line upfly dedupe --json prints when the run finishes: for each set of identical images, the copy kept and the references pointed at it. Without --apply nothing is written and run is null. Nothing is ever deleted: a copy no reference names afterwards stays on disk. Progress lines come before it (events.json); a run that stops or refuses prints an error line instead (events.json).

apply.description: Whether --apply was given, so the plan was written.

sets.description: Each set of images with the same bytes.

rewrites.description: The references that move, one entry per file, in path order.

notes.description: On a dry run, what --apply would refuse, each a sentence.

kept.description: Why that copy: named by --keep (chosen), used by the most references (most-used), in a folder the site is served from (served), the shortest path (shorter), or first in path order (first). Each rule decides only a tie on the ones before it.

copies.description: Every other copy, in path order.

references.description: The references that name it now.

moved.description: How many of them are pointed at the kept copy.

stays.description: The references that stay as written, each with the reason.

unusedAfter.description: true when no reference Upfly can read names it once the plan is written. It stays on disk, and upfly audit then lists it as unused.
